text:
Matvei Gridin is 20, a year and change removed from the QMJHL, and already playing 17 minutes a night for the Flames. His ice time is up almost three minutes over his last ten games, and he has earned it: 11 points in 19 games, five of them on the power play.

The finishing is a little ahead of the chances (5 goals on 3.6 expected goals, which measures the quality of his looks), but not by a worrying amount, and his line has been unlucky the other way when he's on the ice. The skating is real: his top speed sits in the 94th percentile of the league by NHL Edge tracking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries last season, the habit that turns into chances.

The flag to watch is the cold patch: no goals since October 30. For context, forwards picked around 28th overall usually manage about 0.35 points a game in their first real season. He's at 0.58.
headline: Gridin is making the jump look easy
